NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 843 9759 4309 , Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 843 9759 4309 , Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 8, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:01 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Assistant City Attorney Kane Thuyen
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Code Compliance Officer Hall
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING JUNE 2021 "PRIDE MONTH"

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN announced that the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates has declared June, “Pride Month”, and introduced RHE Resident Lisa
  Augustine to say a few words.

  COUNCILMEMBER STEGURA introduced community member, Lisa Augustine, who
  shared her personal experiences with the LGBTQ Community and thanked the City
  Council for recognizing June as “Pride Month”.

B.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE SECOND QUARTER 2021

  Sharon Shapiro-Fox of Waste Management drew names for the 2nd quarter winners
  to receive one free year of service: SECOND QUARTER RESIDENTIAL WINNER:
  71 Buckskin Rd. SECOND QUARTER COMMERCIAL WINNER: New Horizons.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STE GURA,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JUNE 8, 2021
   APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF MAY 2021 AND JUNE 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 63980 THROUGH 64009 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $363,934.87 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 050521 THROUGH
  050621; AND 63980 (VOID) IN THE AMOUNT OF $78,281.69 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $442,216.56 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  PARK & ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 17, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF MAY 24, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  2021 BI-ANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT

  REVIEWED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 210162
  DRAFT HOUSING ELEMENT 2021-2029 LOCATION: CITYWIDE

Planning Manager, Jeannie Naughton, introduced the item (as per the agenda material) and
introduced Surabhi Barbhaya of Michael Baker International to present the report.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN asked if any development plans have been submitted specific to the
Peninsula Center; Planning Manager Naughton stated that no formal plans have been received
but rather there have been discussions regarding a potential future housing project upon
completion of the City’s General Plan and Housing Element.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired regarding lot consolidation, he asked how it relates to a
signage bonus as stated in the report. Ms. Barbhaya noted that it referred to more prominent
signage by the developer.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN spoke regarding the State’s handling of the housing situation starting
with the needs assessment specifically relating to numbers provided by a private consultant at
the direction of the legislature as opposed to the demographers who typically provided the
numbers. He stated this is a serious concern with the numbers from the private consultant
noting they are essentially double the model that the Department of Finance has used in the
past and more importantly are within 10% of the Freddie Mac, Federal model.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN stated that double counting, occupancy rates and using inappropriate
vacancy rates for apartments and for single family homes is the cause of the incorrect counts.
He added that this type of incorrect counting was baked into the model and applied, year after
year. He went on to say that the numbers provided are not tenable.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired regarding the mixed use overlay, and asked staff if the Town
and Country shopping parcel can be made exempt from residential development. Community
Development and Public Works Director Wahba noted that the land was previously zoned 22
units to the acre in the late 1990s through Zoning as well as in the 1992 General Plan.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 8, 2021
 Planning Manager Naughton spoke regarding the passing of SB 330 in 2019 which prohibits
local governments from down-zoning properties.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that she agrees with MAYOR ZUCKERMAN’S
comments and understands that the City has obligations under state law.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN asked staff if the draft Housing Element has been prepared
to be consistent with what the State requires in order to certify it. Community Development and
Public Works Director Wahba responded affirmatively. MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN went
on to say that the problem is not an ideology problem but rather a problem with the math and
supports staff moving forward with sending the draft document to the state for review.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ commended staff for their work and spoke about open space
and the importance of safeguarding it. She added that representatives in Sacramento need to
consider issues such as overgrowth, drought and erosion prior to referring to themselves as
environmentalists. She commended Senator Ben Allen for his thoughtful and representative
voice, and she encouraged him to continue to advocate for things that are important to our
community.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ TO DIRECT STAFF TO TRANSMIT THE DRAFT DOCUMENT TO HCD
  FOR PRELIMINARY REVIEW.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  LETTER OF SUPPORT: BUDGET REQUEST SB 1383 PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT
  AND IMPLEMENTATION FEE

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF
  TO AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SEND A LETTER OF SUPPORT FOR A BUDGET
  REQUEST FOR SB 1383 PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  APPROVAL OF AGREEMENTS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF "BUTCHER PARK"
  PROJECT

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that she is pleased to see the project moving forward and
that it has been a long time coming. She added that staff should expect discussion around a
name change for the park in the near future.

Baxter Miller, President BMLA Landscape Architecture noted the project is a simple one but
rather the larger issue is dealing with challenges around the rising costs of materials and labor.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 8, 2021
 City Council and staff discussion ensued regarding storm water obligation and how it may
impact the bid price; the question was raised if it is premature to enter into a bid tonight. Staff
responded that BMLA Landscape Architect will be developing the plan prior to going out to bid
and does not anticipate any issues with approval of the PSA as proposed.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ TO
  APPROVE A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH BMLA LANDSCAPE
  ARCHITECTS IN THE AMOUNT OF $12,515 FOR PROJECT PLANS AND
  SPECIFICATIONS AND A TASK ORDER WITH WILDAN ENGINEERING FOR A
  SURVEY AND CIVIL PLANS, PROJECT MANAGEMENT, BIDDING AND
  CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $25,738, UPON CITY
  ATTORNEY FINAL REVIEW.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that in Rolling Hills Estates those 16 years of age and older
are now at about a 78% vaccination rate, and for seniors 65 and over, the rates are about
95%. He noted that in both categories, RHE is in the top five of LA County. City Manager
Grammer commended residents for being proactive. He added that on June 15, the state is
going to be lifting capacity, social distancing, and masking requirements at businesses and
the County then will align with the state in order to allow businesses to fully reopen. He
added that although the state's blueprint for a safer economy is going to come to an end on
June 15, the Governor has extended his emergency executive order to allow legislative
bodies to continue to meet by teleconference and continue to comply with the Brown Act.
The Cal OSHA Standards Board met last week and is recommending relaxing the social
distancing and masking requirements for fully vaccinated workers to be in line with the June
15 reopening date. If approved by the State Office of Administrative Law, within the next 10
days, it is expected to go into effect on June 15. He noted that RHE staff would be required
to follow Cal OSHA standards. He added that when all employees are fully vaccinated, and
have no symptoms, they will not be required to wear face coverings in a room where
everyone's fully vaccinated. However, if there is anyone that is not vaccinated, then face
coverings are required for everyone, regardless of vaccination status. City Manager
Grammer suggested that perhaps the June 22 City Council meeting could be held in person
noting that staff has been preparing for that. He added the option of using the patio to
accommodate attendees, but noted that to be in compliance with Cal OSHA, if even one
member of the public attends the meeting, everyone may need to wear masks. He
suggested placing a podium on the patio and encouraging attendees to sit outside while still
able to participate. He provided City Council the option to meet in person on June 22 but
reminded them that the Governor’s Emergency Executive Order, allowed for the
continuation of virtual meetings.

Discussion ensued and Council consensus was to continue to hold virtual meetings through
June 22.

  RECEIVED AND FILED SO ORDERED BY MAYOR ZUCKERMAN

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

City Council Reports:

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported having attended the Palos Verdes (PV) Chamber of
Commerce Economic Development Committee and shared information regarding their
upcoming Peninsula Business Fair to be held at the Peninsula Center on the weekend of
June 19 and 20. She added that there will be a carnival starting on Friday afternoon June 18,
running through Sunday June 20. She encouraged PV businesses to register and provide
booths to advertise their businesses. She noted that this would be a good opportunity for
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 8, 2021
 people to come and use RHE restaurants on the Hill. She extend an invitation from the
Chamber for everyone who's available to attend

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported having attended a reception at the Los Angeles
County Division, League of California Cities noting Secretary of State Treasurer, Fiona Ma
as guest speaker.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN encouraged members of the public to contact the Chamber if
interested in volunteering at the Peninsula Business Fair carnival.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA reported having attended the League of California Cities
Transportation Communication Public Works Committee meeting last week. She shared
topics discussed including anticipated Federal Government COVID monies to cities, she
added that a new lobbyist is working with the League whom provided an extensive report
and noted there was an action item asking for support or not on AB 122, a piece of legislation
that would permit bicyclists to pause at a stop sign, rather than stop when they come through
an intersection so they do not need to come out of their clips. She added that if traffic is
coming, then they would be required to stop. Discussion ensued regarding whether to
support or not support this piece of legislation, reporting that votes were about three quarters
yes to support and about one quarter voting not to support it. COUNCIL MEMBER
STEGURA shared having voted against supporting AB 122, adding that although this
legislation may be safer for bicyclists, she felt it is not so for pedestrians or vehicles.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN provided his own cycling experiences and personal support
for the legislation.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN reported having attended the Clean Power Alliance Board Meeting
noting approval of four power purchase agreements that will provide enough power for
almost 200,000 homes, in addition to what’s already been purchased will allow for the
removal of over a million metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions per year. He stated that
RHE is one of two cities along with the County that got this ball rolling adding that RHE was
foundational in the CPA by initially working with the county attorney noting that the county
had previously lent $10 million all of which has been paid back. He added that we should all
be proud that our City really has done a lot for a city of any size and a million tons of carbon
savings is pretty impressive.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

NONE.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS Government Code Section 54957.6

Tuesday, June 22, 2021 at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference.

Carrie Gallagher, CMC  Steve Zuckerman
